title: Negation-invariance of bad restrictions
statement: Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function, $d$ a natural number, and $\rho$ a restriction on the $n$ variables. Then $\rho$ is bad for the negation $\lnot f$ at depth $d$ if and only if $\rho$ is bad for $f$ at depth $d$; that is, the restricted function of $\lnot f$ under $\rho$ has decision-tree depth greater than $d$ exactly when the restricted function of $f$ under $\rho$ does.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
d is a natural number (the depth threshold)
ρ is a restriction on the n variables
